1	---
2	name: dogfood
3	primitive: P11
4	category: governance
5	description: "Per-bstack-P11 reflex 7+16 — explicitly trigger the Dogfood Plan + per-stack cookbook + Dogfood Receipt sequence. Auto-detects the tech stack from repo signals (Cargo.toml + src-tauri/ → tauri-sidecar; next.config.* → nextjs; app.json + expo → expo-rn; Cargo.toml solo → rust-cli; openapi.* or REST framework deps → rest-api; mcp.{json,yaml} → mcp-server), loads the matching cookbook entry from bstack/references/dogfood-patterns.md (broomva/bstack ≥ 0.13.0), produces a six-row Dogfood Plan (entry surface · driver · evidence · smoke · end-to-end · receipt anchor), optionally executes via the named surfaces (Interceptor mandatory for visual deploy verification; gstack, cliclick, screencapture, curl+jq, xcrun simctl compose per stack), and produces the final receipt with binary anti-rationalization check. Three subcommands: /dogfood (full sequence — plan → execute → receipt), /dogfood plan (plan only), /dogfood receipt (receipt only, assumes plan exists in PR body or AGENTS.md). Inherits from broomva/bstack: cookbook, P11 discipline, stack-detection algorithm. Composes with broomva/autonomous (which fires this implicitly at reflex 7+16) — use /dogfood directly for narrower scope (small changes, exploration, pre-merge verification gate without full pipeline). USE WHEN dogfood, dogfood this, dogfood plan, dogfood receipt, validate as user, exercise the change, click through the app, /dogfood, P11 receipt, exercise like a user would, did I actually click it, prove this works for a user, interaction evidence, deploy verification. NOT FOR running CI checks (use /p9), batch headless automation (use Browser skill), or scientific-method experiment framing (use Science skill)."
6	argument-hint: [plan|execute|receipt|--stack=<name>|--ticket=<id>|--evidence-dir=<path>]
7	effort: low
8	---
9	
10	# dogfood — explicit P11 reflex trigger (Dogfood Plan + Receipt)
11	
12	Explicit trigger for **bstack P11 reflex 7+16** for: **$ARGUMENTS**
13	
14	## Inheritance from bstack (declared)
15	
16	This skill is downstream of [`broomva/bstack`](https://github.com/broomva/bstack). It implements P11 reflex 7 (Dogfood Plan keyed to detected stack) and reflex 16 (Dogfood Receipt) explicitly, where `/autonomous` fires them implicitly inside its 21-reflex pipeline. Full inheritance contract: [`references/bstack-inheritance.md`](references/bstack-inheritance.md).
17	
18	- **Cookbook source**: `bstack/references/dogfood-patterns.md` (loaded on demand; not duplicated here)
19	- **Discipline source**: `bstack/references/primitives.md` §P11
20	- **Stack-detection algorithm**: mirrors `bstack/scripts/doctor.sh` §13
21	- **Minimum bstack version**: 0.13.0
22	
23	If bstack isn't installed, the skill still works — it carries its own detection logic and inlines the minimum surfaces matrix. The *cookbook* (deep per-stack reference) lives upstream in bstack.
24	
25	## Purpose
26	
27	P11 (Empirical Feedback Loop) mandates *"before claiming work complete, the agent has interacted with the deployed/running version… reasoning isn't validation; interaction is."* This skill makes the two binding reflexes (Plan + Receipt) explicitly triggerable when you don't want the full `/autonomous` pipeline.
28	
29	When to invoke `/dogfood` instead of `/autonomous`:
30	- Single-file change with user-visible effect
31	- Exploration: "what does dogfooding look like for this stack"
32	- Pre-merge verification gate on someone else's PR
33	- First time seeing a tech stack you're new to (cookbook entry is the answer)
34	- Receipt-only after manual execution
35	
36	## Usage
37	
38	```
39	/dogfood                        # full sequence: plan → execute prompt → receipt
40	/dogfood plan                   # plan only — produce the six-row plan
41	/dogfood execute                # execute — fire the surfaces named in the plan
42	/dogfood receipt                # receipt only — produce the evidence table
43	/dogfood --stack=tauri-sidecar  # override detection
44	/dogfood --ticket=BRO-1234      # anchor evidence path to ticket
45	/dogfood --evidence-dir=/tmp/dogfood/<slug>
46	```
47	
48	CLI fallback (no Claude session required):
49	
50	```bash
51	./scripts/dogfood.sh detect              # echo detected stack
52	./scripts/dogfood.sh plan --stack=nextjs # emit plan template stub
53	./scripts/dogfood.sh receipt --plan=plan.md
54	```
55	
56	## Workflow
57	
58	### Phase 1 — Detect stack
59	
60	Mirror `bstack/scripts/doctor.sh` §13 detection. If `--stack=<name>` was passed, use that instead. If detection returns `unknown`, the agent declares the stack explicitly in the plan (no silent default).
61	
62	```bash
63	./scripts/dogfood.sh detect
64	# → tauri-sidecar | nextjs | expo-rn | rust-cli | rest-api | mcp-server | unknown
65	```
66	
67	The detection logic mirrors what `bstack doctor §13` does. If `bstack doctor` is installed and recent, prefer its output:
68	
69	```bash
70	if command -v bstack >/dev/null 2>&1; then
71	    bstack doctor 2>&1 | grep "^  \[ok\] stack detected:" | sed 's/.*stack detected: //; s/ .*//'
72	fi
73	```
74	
75	### Phase 2 — Load cookbook entry
76	
77	Read the matching pattern section from `bstack/references/dogfood-patterns.md`:
78	
79	```bash
80	# Section IDs in the cookbook:
81	#   Pattern A — Tauri + sidecar
82	#   Pattern B — Next.js
83	#   Pattern C — Expo / React Native
84	#   Pattern D — Rust CLI
85	#   Pattern E — REST API
86	#   Pattern F — MCP server / Tool provider
87	
88	BSTACK_REF=$(npx skills path broomva/bstack 2>/dev/null || echo "$HOME/.agents/skills/bstack")
89	COOKBOOK="$BSTACK_REF/references/dogfood-patterns.md"
90	```
91	
92	If the cookbook isn't reachable (bstack not installed or older than v0.13.0), fall back to the **minimum surfaces table** inlined below in `Phase 2 — fallback (no bstack)`. The agent surfaces a one-line warning recommending bstack installation for the deep cookbook.
93	
94	### Phase 2 — fallback (no bstack ≥ 0.13.0 available)
95	
96	Minimum surfaces table (covers ~80% of cases without the deep cookbook):
97	
98	| Stack | Primary surfaces | Mandatory |
99	|---|---|---|
100	| tauri-sidecar | curl+jq engine API · cliclick+screencapture · Interceptor at :1420 | Interceptor for visual verification |
101	| nextjs | dev server log-tail · Interceptor · curl+jq for routes | Interceptor for authenticated flows |
102	| expo-rn | `expo start --ios` · `xcrun simctl io booted screenshot` | Simulator screenshots |
103	| rust-cli | direct invocation · `--help` smoke · trycmd/assert_cmd | Exit code 0 + output capture |
104	| rest-api | curl+jq · log-tail · OpenAPI diff if applicable | Response body assertion |
105	| mcp-server | `npx @modelcontextprotocol/inspector` or direct LLM invoke | Tool-call response capture |
106	
107	For deeper detail (canonical arc, bash snippets, gotchas, receipt template): install bstack ≥ 0.13.0.
108	
109	### Phase 3 — Produce the Dogfood Plan
110	
111	Surface the plan in the agent's response, and (if a PR is active) into the PR body via `gh pr edit <pr> --body-file` or `gh pr comment <pr>`. Six rows, all mandatory:
112	
113	```markdown
114	**Dogfood Plan** (stack: <detected>, ticket: <id-or-none>)
115	
116	- **Entry surface**: <URL / window / CLI command the user touches>
117	- **Driver**: <Interceptor / gstack / cliclick+screencapture / curl+jq / xcrun simctl>
118	- **Evidence**: <screenshot path / response body path / log line / recording>
119	- **Smoke**: <one-line "didn't obviously break" check>
120	- **End-to-end**: <multi-step user flow that catches regression a smoke test misses>
121	- **Receipt anchor**: <file / line / PR comment ID where the receipt lives>
122	```
123	
124	The plan rows MUST be concrete — file paths, URLs, commands, not vibes. Rows that genuinely don't apply are marked `⊘` with explicit reason ("backend mocked in this PR; real cloud creds not available — smoke-only this run"). Silent omission is the failure mode this contract closes.
125	
126	### Phase 4 — Execute (only if subcommand is `execute` / `explore` or full sequence)
127	
128	For each plan row, fire the named driver. The `explore` subcommand (v0.2.0+) emits the per-stack execution recipe; for web stacks it composes with the agent-browser exploratory workflow.
129	
130	#### Exploratory web QA mode (v0.2.0+)
131	
132	For web stacks (`nextjs`, `rest-api`-with-frontend, or any `--url=` target), `/dogfood explore --url=...` produces an **agent-browser session-based exploration recipe**: initialize → authenticate → orient → explore → document issues → wrap up. Each issue logged with screenshots / video / repro-steps to `./dogfood-output/<slug>/`. The exploratory output's `report.md` becomes the parent Dogfood Plan's *Evidence* row.
133	
134	```bash
135	dogfood explore --url=https://staging.example.com --session=billing-page --ticket=BRO-1234
136	# → emits a recipe: agent-browser open · snapshot · screenshot · errors · console
137	# → mkdir -p ./dogfood-output/staging-example-com/{screenshots,videos}
138	# → cp templates/exploratory-report.md → output dir
139	```
140	
141	**Composition with the upstream `dogfood` skill**: the agent-browser workflow + issue taxonomy + report template are adapted from the pre-existing `dogfood` skill at `~/.agents/skills/dogfood/` (agent-skills catalog). See `references/bstack-inheritance.md` for attribution + `references/exploratory-issue-taxonomy.md` for what to look for.
142	
143	#### Per-stack execution snippets
144	
145	**tauri-sidecar**:
146	```bash
147	osascript -e 'tell application "Houston" to activate'
148	cliclick c:1662,1090
149	cliclick t:"My test mission"
150	cliclick kp:return
151	sleep 1
152	screencapture -x -t png -R 1480,200,470,980 "$EVIDENCE_DIR/after-input.png"
153	```
154	
155	**nextjs**:
156	```bash
157	interceptor open "http://localhost:3000/<route>"
158	interceptor read --max-tokens 4000
159	interceptor act --click "Submit"
160	interceptor wait-stable
161	interceptor screenshot "$EVIDENCE_DIR/after-submit.png"
162	```
163	
164	**rest-api**:
165	```bash
166	curl -sS -X POST "$BASE/api/<route>" \
167	  -H 'content-type: application/json' \
168	  -d '{"foo":"bar"}' | jq . | tee "$EVIDENCE_DIR/response.json"
169	```
170	
171	Capture the exit status of each driver invocation. Failed invocations are surfaced before producing the receipt.
172	
173	### Phase 5 — Produce the Dogfood Receipt
174	
175	After execution (or after the user reports manual execution), produce the evidence table:
176	
177	```markdown
178	**Dogfood Receipt** — <ticket> · <date>
179	
180	| Plan row | Executed | Evidence |
181	|---|---|---|
182	| Smoke | ✅ | <evidence>: <path / output line> |
183	| End-to-end | ✅ | Screenshots: <paths> |
184	| API contract | ✅ | <response captured in PR comment #N> |
185	| Side-effect | ✅ | <DB query / log / state assertion> |
186	| Deploy preview | ✅ | <preview URL> — Interceptor screenshot <path> |
187	| <row that wasn't applicable> | ⊘ | Reason: <explicit> |
188	
189	**Anti-rationalization check**: did I actually click the app like a user would? <yes/no>
190	**Surfaces driven**: <Interceptor / cliclick / curl / etc.>
191	**Time-to-receipt**: <duration> from first write to receipt complete.
192	```
193	
194	The **anti-rationalization line is binary and mandatory**. If the honest answer is no, the receipt isn't complete — the plan goes back into execution.
195	
196	### Phase 6 — Persist the receipt
197	
198	Anchor the receipt at the location named in the plan's *Receipt anchor* row:
199	
200	- **PR body** — `gh pr comment <pr> --body "$(cat receipt.md)"` OR include in PR description
201	- **Repo file** — `docs/dogfood-receipts/<date>-<ticket>.md` for repos with substantial dogfood history
202	- **Bridge (P1) auto-capture** — bstack's Stop hook captures the session-end receipt to Obsidian automatically; no explicit action needed if bstack is installed
203	
204	## Composition with /autonomous
205	
206	`/autonomous` fires this skill at reflex 7 (Plan) and reflex 16 (Receipt). When invoked directly, `/dogfood` runs in isolation. Both produce the same artifacts; the difference is scope.
207	
208	| Scope | Use |
209	|---|---|
210	| Full feature work (multi-file, public contract, deploy-impacting) | `/autonomous` |
211	| Single-file change with user-visible effect | `/dogfood` directly |
212	| Pre-merge verification of someone else's PR | `/dogfood --ticket=<id>` |
213	| First time seeing a new tech stack | `/dogfood plan` |
214	| Receipt-only after manual execution | `/dogfood receipt` |
215	
216	## Anti-patterns this skill closes
217	
218	| Anti-pattern | Why it fails | What `/dogfood` enforces |
219	|---|---|---|
220	| "Compile-time pass = shipping" | Compile ≠ deploy correctness | Plan rows require evidence beyond exit codes |
221	| "CI green = shipping" | CI tests what CI was told; user flow is broader | Receipt requires deploy-verification screenshot |
222	| "I dogfooded mentally" | Ritual without artifact | Receipt table is the artifact; anti-rationalization line is binary |
223	| "I'll dogfood after merge" | Post-merge = bug found by user | Plan precedes substantive work; receipt precedes claiming complete |
224	| Agent-browser for visual deploy verification | Bot detection + missed visual state | Interceptor mandatory per cookbook |
225	
226	## Cross-references
227	
228	- **Cookbook (per-stack patterns)**: `bstack/references/dogfood-patterns.md` (loaded on demand)
229	- **P11 reflex contract**: `bstack/references/primitives.md` §P11
230	- **Inheritance declaration**: [`references/bstack-inheritance.md`](references/bstack-inheritance.md)
231	- **Interceptor skill**: `~/.claude/skills/Interceptor/SKILL.md`
232	- **`/autonomous` skill**: [`broomva/autonomous`](https://github.com/broomva/autonomous) (composes this skill at reflex 7+16)
233	
234	## Voice notification (optional, for environments that support it)
235	
236	If a local voice-notification daemon is running on port 31337:
237	
238	```bash
239	curl -s -X POST http://localhost:31337/notify \
240	  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
241	  -d '{"message": "Running the dogfood skill — producing P11 plan + receipt for the detected stack"}' \
242	  > /dev/null 2>&1 &
243	```
244	
245	Skip silently if the daemon isn't running.
